g.text: DMX512-A at 250 kbaud — the frame layer, and the one counted cell every byte uses
FRAME LAYER — break, mark, start code, 512 slots
THE BREAK
LDI A,0 / OUT TXPIN — the line going LOW IS the break
LDI A,22 / STM 6,A
117 iterations of a 2-instruction body plus
236 clocks of delay = 240 clocks per iteration
THE MARK
LDI A,1 / OUT TXPIN — released ONCE, here, not in
the loop: an OUT inside it would make the mark
depend on which iteration it was
THE START CODE
dmem[7] = 0, dmem[8] = 0x00
it goes out through the SAME transmitter as
the data slots, so there is one bit format in
this file and not two
first_data
dmem[1] = 0, dmem[2] = 0, dmem[9] = 0
THE PAGE COUNTER, and this line is the whole
difference between a frame that ends and a
transmitter that runs for ever. It was left
uninitialised, so at the first page boundary
it was x, x+1 is x, and SUB A,2 on an x is an
x: the frame never stopped
slots
dmem[8] = dmem[2] (the slot value IS the ramp)
dmem[7] = 1 (this one IS a data slot)
slot_done
dmem[2] + 1 (8 bits, so this wraps at 255 by itself)
dmem[1] + 1 / JZ page_end
THE PAGE COUNTER IS NOT INCREMENTED HERE,
and the first version did it on every slot,
which ended the frame after TWO data slots —
because 2 was the page count and the page
counter was being asked to count slots
page_end
dmem[9] + 1 / SUB A,2 / JZ done
512 data slots = 2 pages of 256
done
dmem[10] = 0xA5
park
TRANSMITTER — 250 kbaud, 8N2, one loop over ELEVEN bit cells
sbit — the dispatch, and its four different lengths
LDM A,5 / SUB A,9 / JZ sb_stop
SUB A,1 / JZ sb_stop2 / JZ sb_start
cells 1-8: 7 instructions of dispatch then LDM+AND+OUT
cell 0: the same 7, the last JZ taken
cell 9: 2 instructions of dispatch, then LDI+OUT
cell 10: 3 of dispatch, then LDI+OUT
the DATA branch
LDM A,0 / AND A,1 / OUT TXPIN — LSB first
then LDM/SHR/STM: the shift lives HERE and
not in the common tail. On a ramp the LOW
bits are the difference between a fixture
that works and one that does not
sb_start — cell 0
LDI A,0 / OUT TXPIN
3 NOPs. This dispatch is one instruction
shorter than a data cell's, and the cell that
has to be 240 clocks is the DATA cell after
it, not this one
sb_stop — cell 9
5 NOPs: the shortest dispatch in the file, and
the cell it must make correct is cell 8.
Then LDI A,1 / OUT, then 2 NOPs, for
cell 9 rather than this one
sb_stop2 — cell 10
4 NOPs, and they are here for cell 9's sake,
not this cell's. FALLS THROUGH into sb_hold:
this is the last cell of a slot, so it has
no successor whose length has to match
sb_hold
LDI A,109 (1 clock) then SUB A,1 / JNZ
4.000 us = exactly 250,000 baud
218 = 2 x 109 and 109 is prime: this or a
109-instruction body run twice, which is the
same arithmetic written in 107 NOPs
dmem[4]--, dmem[5]++
slot_out — ONE EXIT FOR ALL 513 SLOTS
NO RETURN POINT AND NO DISPATCH: the frame layer
JMPs in and this block falls out of the
transmitter's last cell, so the continuation IS
the program counter. Noticing that the control
flow already provides the thing the ISA lacks is
worth more than the dmem slot would have been.
dmem[3]++ then dmem[7] decides what leaving means
THE START CODE'S EXIT MUST NOT ADVANCE THE
RAMP. The payload is deliberately "data slot k
has value k", so the first data slot is 0x00,
and an exit that advanced the ramp on the way
past the start code would make the first data
slot 0x01 and the payload "k + 1" - still a
ramp, still a legal fixture, and one index out
of step with every document describing it. The
first version had exactly that bug and the TB
caught it as a single mismatched slot, which is
the cheapest possible way to catch an
off-by-one in a 513-slot frame.
not a page boundary
256 slots
dmem[9] < 2
dmem[9] == 2
dmem[7] = 1
dmem[7] = 0, the start code's exit
